title: Sparse-Blossom Decoding in $o(1)$ Time
summary: Matching-based decoding is widely used in quantum error correction, and accelerating it is key to enabling fast and scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation. Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) decoding provides rigorous guarantees for error suppression, while sparse blossom enables its practical implementation at modest problem sizes. However, the runtime of existing sparse-blossom implementations unavoidably increases with problem size, motivating a rigorous parallelization framework that guarantees correctness and a runtime shorter than the syndrome-extraction timescale.
